body.statement: Every returned certificate \(\kappa_H\) is sound over \(\Theta_H\). On a formula branch, the registry contains every context normalizer, reachable fixing margin, and reduced rational-elimination denominator together with its positivity-ledger factorization; \(O_H(\Theta_H)\subseteq\mathfrak D_H\), and \(F_H\{O_H(\theta)\}=T_{a,H}(\theta)\) for every \(\theta\in\Theta_H\). No value is asserted outside \(\mathfrak D_H\). On a negative branch, for every \(b\in\mathcal B_H\), \(\theta_b^{+},\theta_b^{-}\in\Theta_H\), \(O_H(\theta_b^{+})=O_H(\theta_b^{-})\), and \(T_{a,H}(\theta_b^{+})\ne T_{a,H}(\theta_b^{-})\); both laws have selector support exactly \(H\) and strictly positive structurally admissible cells.
body.justification: A failed search becomes an exact, auditable nonidentification result instead of an inconclusive token.
body.gap: The 2024 anchor proves witnesses for specified failures but does not furnish a fixed-support global pair on every residual branch or an open family of legal pairs.
body.consumer: A provenance-aware do-search backend can return machine-checkable formulas or legal missing-context and twin diagnostics.
body.proof_tex:
Let a certificate be returned, and first work in the normalized parameterization.  By \(\textnormal{thm:normalization-equivalence}\), every \(\theta\in\Theta_H\) has the unique normalized representative \(\eta=\nu_H(\theta)\in\mathcal I_H\), and
\[
 O_H^N(\eta)=O_H(\theta),\qquad
 T_{a,H}^N(\eta)=T_{a,H}(\theta).
\tag{1}
\]
Every transition used to obtain the certificate is admitted only after the exact local obligations in \(\textnormal{def:sa-csid-machine}\) have succeeded.  We record why these obligations are sufficient.  At a selector transition, the stored zero--one multiplexer equation makes replacement by \(\mathbf 1\{X=x_s\}\), followed by substitution of \(x_s\) in the children, an equality of the two context-kernel polynomials modulo the inherited gate and coordinate-copy constraints.  This rewrite creates no divisor.  At a fixing transition the successor is \(K'_{s,D}=K_{s,D}/m_{s,W}\), and the verified identity is
\[
 m_{s,W}K'_{s,D}=K_{s,D}.
\tag{2}
\]
At a sum or district transition, the corresponding expanded identity is likewise verified after multiplication by all reduced denominators.  The positivity ledger makes every such multiplication reversible on the registered branch domain.  Induction over the finite returned transition log therefore shows that its final labelled circuits represent the same observation--target relation as the initial normalized circuits on that domain.  This uses only the exact polynomial identities required by the four transition definitions; it does not infer an identity from graphical eligibility alone.

Consider a formula certificate.  Write the accepted residual candidate as \(F_H=P/D\), where \(D\) is the product of its sign-normalized reduced denominators.  Reduction to zero modulo the current finite constraint list \(\mathcal J=(J_1,\ldots,J_M)\) means that the verifier has polynomial multipliers \(h_1,\ldots,h_M\) for which the formal identity
\[
 D\,t_{a,H}^N-P(o_H^N)=\sum_{j=1}^M h_jJ_j
\tag{3}
\]
holds componentwise.  For \(\eta=\nu_H(\theta)\in\mathcal I_H\), every inherited constraint \(J_j(\eta)\) is zero by the construction of the current constraint list from \(\mathcal I_H\).  Thus the right side of (3) vanishes at \(\eta\).  By \(\textnormal{lem:restricted-support-denominator-positivity}\), every selector normalizer, fixing margin, and admitted elimination denominator is strictly positive at \(O_H^N(\eta)=O_H(\theta)\).  Consequently
\[
 O_H(\Theta_H)\subseteq\mathfrak D_H,
\qquad
 D\{O_H^N(\eta)\}>0.
\tag{4}
\]
Division of (3) by the positive value in (4), followed by (1), gives
\[
 F_H\{O_H(\theta)\}
 =F_H\{O_H^N(\eta)\}
 =T_{a,H}^N(\eta)
 =T_{a,H}(\theta)
\quad(\theta\in\Theta_H).
\tag{5}
\]
The definition of \(F_H\) has domain \(\mathfrak D_H\), so (5) makes no assertion at an ambient table outside that domain.

Now consider a negative certificate and fix \(b\in\mathcal B_H\).  Let \(\eta_b^+\) and \(\eta_b^-\) denote the two normalized primitive records to which the residual transition applies \(\rho_H\).  This application is well typed only on \(\mathcal I_H\), because \(\rho_H:\mathcal I_H\to\Theta_H\); hence an admitted and returned residual transition has
\[
 \eta_b^+,\eta_b^-\in\mathcal I_H,
 \qquad
 \theta_b^\pm:=\rho_H(\eta_b^\pm)\in\Theta_H.
\tag{6}
\]
Concretely, the verifier establishes (6) by its primitive-simplex signs, the equalities in the retained constraint list, the selector-mass signs
\[
 s_H^N(\eta_b^\pm)(s)>0\iff s\in H,
\tag{7}
\]
and strict positivity of every admissible observation polynomial.  Thus neither support nor root-factorization membership is inferred merely from observed-law equality.

The two remaining accepted residual obligations are polynomial equality of all supported observed coordinates and a target-difference polynomial of certified nonzero constant sign on the open rational box.  Therefore
\[
 O_H^N(\eta_b^+)=O_H^N(\eta_b^-),
 \qquad
 T_{a,H}^N(\eta_b^+)\ne T_{a,H}^N(\eta_b^-).
\tag{8}
\]
Applying the two inverse identities from \(\textnormal{thm:normalization-equivalence}\) to (6)--(8) yields
\[
 O_H(\theta_b^+)=O_H(\theta_b^-),
 \qquad
 T_{a,H}(\theta_b^+)\ne T_{a,H}(\theta_b^-).
\tag{9}
\]
Finally, membership in \(\Theta_H\) in (6), together with \(\textnormal{ass:exact-selector-support}\) and \(\textnormal{ass:admissible-cell-interior}\), says that both models have selector support exactly \(H\) and every structurally admissible supported cell is strictly positive.  Equations (4)--(5) and (6)--(9) prove the two asserted soundness alternatives.
